description: Judgments of the LLM judge that a human reviewed. An entry whose human_verdict differs from judge_verdict is an override: reports show accuracy as judged and after these corrections. All entries (agreements too) are used to estimate judge reliability.
notes: match: fields a result row must have (method, id, and for needle results length_target and position).

judge: which judge produced the verdict. 'whole-paper v1' = original rules (run 1); 'whole-paper v2' = approved rules used in run 2 and eval/run_ask.py; 'excerpts' = eval/judge.py used by eval/run_needle.py.
reviewed_by: 'user' = decided by the user; 'claude' = checked by Claude against the paper text during the session and reported to the user.

The reviewed judgments were mostly chosen because they looked suspicious (incorrect verdicts, unusual answers), so reliability computed from them is a pessimistic, biased estimate, not a random sample.

Known judge bias (accepted as a limitation): the judges err mostly by being too strict and rarely by being too lenient. Too strict: judge 'whole-paper v2' can mark a correct no_consensus answer incorrect because it contains true extra details (q20 in three runs); rewording the rule (v3) and a structured judge were tried in calibration and did not fix it reliably, so the judge stays at v2. Too lenient: the 'excerpts' judge marked q23 correct in three 64k needle runs although the answer gave an unsupported number and its own reason said so. All such cases are corrected here.
